AGN_002.title: The operator has no name
AGN_002.what: An operator in the operator list has no name; riders cannot see who runs the service.
AGN_002.action: Enter the operator name riders know.

AGN_003.title: The agency's website address is invalid
AGN_003.what: The website address provided for {agency} is not a valid URL.
AGN_003.action: Enter a valid website address for the agency.

AGN_004.title: Operator time zone missing or invalid
AGN_004.what: The operator has no time zone or an unrecognised one; apps may shift trip times to the wrong hour.
AGN_004.action: Enter the time zone with its standard name, such as "Europe/Istanbul".

AGN_005.title: Operators use different time zones
AGN_005.what: Operators in the dataset use different time zones; in one dataset they must all be the same.
AGN_005.action: Give all operators the same time zone.

AGN_006.title: Operator language invalid
AGN_006.what: The language code entered for the operator is not recognised.
AGN_006.action: Enter the language with a standard code such as "tr" or "en".

AGN_007.title: Operator phone invalid
AGN_007.what: The phone number entered for the operator does not look like a number.
AGN_007.action: Enter the full number with area code, or leave it empty.

AGN_008.title: Fare page address invalid
AGN_008.what: The address of the operator’s fare information page is not a valid web address.
AGN_008.action: Enter a full address starting with "https://", or leave it empty.

AGN_009.title: Operator e-mail invalid
AGN_009.what: The e-mail address entered for the operator is not valid.
AGN_009.action: Enter the e-mail as name@domain.com, or leave it empty.

AGN_010.title: Same operator code used twice
AGN_010.what: Two operators carry the same code; it becomes unclear which operator a route belongs to.
AGN_010.action: Give each operator a unique code, or merge the duplicate records.

AGN_011.title: Route or fare not linked to an operator
AGN_011.what: There are several operators, but some routes or fares do not say which operator they belong to.
AGN_011.action: Link every route and fare to its operator.

AGN_012.title: Contactless payment value invalid
AGN_012.what: The value saying whether the operator accepts contactless cards is not one of the defined options.

AGN_013.title: Dataset language and operator language differ
AGN_013.what: The language of the dataset does not match the language entered for the operator.
AGN_013.action: Make the two languages the same; if the operator really uses a different language, this is fine.

AGN_014.title: Operator code missing with several operators
AGN_014.what: There is more than one operator but some have no code; routes cannot be linked to them.
AGN_014.action: Give each operator a unique code.

AGN_015.title: Operator address is not secure (http)
AGN_015.what: The operator’s web address starts with "http://"; browsers may show a not-secure warning.
AGN_015.action: If the site supports it, change the address to "https://".

AGN_016.title: Operator phone looks like a placeholder
AGN_016.what: The operator phone is a known test or placeholder number; riders may not reach anyone.
AGN_016.action: Enter the real customer service number.

AGN_017.title: Operators declare different languages
AGN_017.what: Operators in the dataset declare different languages. This is for information.
AGN_017.action: If the network is multilingual this is fine; otherwise use the same language.

AGN_018.title: The only operator has no code
AGN_018.what: There is a single operator and its code is empty. This is harmless now but becomes a problem when a second operator is added.

ARC_001.title: The dataset file cannot be opened
ARC_001.what: The uploaded ZIP file could not be opened; nothing inside it could be read.
ARC_001.action: Export the dataset again from your scheduling software. This is a file format issue; tell the export software vendor or your IT team.

ARC_002.title: Characters in a file cannot be read
ARC_002.what: A file is not in UTF-8 encoding; letters such as ğ, ş, ı in stop and route names may look broken and the file could not be fully checked.
ARC_002.action: Choose UTF-8 as the character encoding when exporting. This is a file format issue; tell the export software vendor or your IT team.

ARC_003.title: Encoding error in an optional file
ARC_003.what: An optional file is not in UTF-8 encoding; the names in it may look broken.
ARC_003.action: Choose UTF-8 as the character encoding when exporting. This is a file format issue; tell the export software vendor or your IT team.

ARC_004.title: Required file is missing
ARC_004.what: A required GTFS file is missing.
ARC_004.action: Add the missing file to the dataset.

ARC_006.title: An optional GTFS file is present
ARC_006.what: The dataset contains an optional file defined by the standard. This is for information.

ARC_007.title: Unrecognised file
ARC_007.what: The dataset contains a file that is not part of the GTFS standard; some apps may ignore it.
ARC_007.action: Check whether the file is needed; if not, leave it out of the export.

ARC_008.title: Service calendar files are missing
ARC_008.what: A file that defines the service calendar is missing.
ARC_008.action: Add the service calendar files to the dataset.

ARC_009.title: Optional file is empty
ARC_009.what: An optional file contains only the header row and no records.
ARC_009.action: If there is nothing to put in it, leave the file out of the export.

ARC_010.title: Invisible mark at the start of the file
ARC_010.what: The file starts with an invisible encoding mark (BOM); most apps read it, some may misname the first column.
ARC_010.action: Use the "UTF-8 without BOM" option when exporting. This is a file format issue; tell the export software vendor or your IT team.

ARC_011.title: File size
ARC_011.what: The size of the files in the dataset is shown for information.

ARC_012.title: File row structure is invalid
ARC_012.what: A row in {file} has a different number of fields than its header.
ARC_012.action: Correct the row and export the file again.

ARC_013.title: File rows cannot be read
ARC_013.what: Quotes, commas or line endings in a file are broken, so rows cannot be split correctly.
ARC_013.action: Export the dataset again. This is a file format issue; tell the export software vendor or your IT team.

ARC_014.title: Spaces in column names
ARC_014.what: Column names in a file’s header row have spaces at the start or end; some apps may not recognise the column.
ARC_014.action: This is a file format issue; tell the export software vendor or your IT team.

ARC_015.title: The same column appears twice
ARC_015.what: The same column name appears twice in a file; apps cannot tell which one to read.
ARC_015.action: This is a file format issue; tell the export software vendor or your IT team.

ARC_017.title: Non-standard column
ARC_017.what: A file has a column not defined in the GTFS standard; some apps may ignore it.
ARC_017.action: If the column is a deliberate addition this is fine; otherwise leave it out of the export.

ARC_018.title: Empty row
ARC_018.what: A file contains a completely empty row.
ARC_018.action: This is a file format issue; tell the export software vendor or your IT team.

ARC_019.title: Column name is empty
ARC_019.what: A file’s header row has a column without a name, usually caused by an extra comma.
ARC_019.action: This is a file format issue; tell the export software vendor or your IT team.

ARC_020.title: Recommended file missing
ARC_020.what: The dataset has no route shapes file or no dataset information file (publisher, validity dates).
ARC_020.action: Add the route shapes and the dataset information to the export.

ARC_021.title: Invisible characters in text
ARC_021.what: Some fields contain special characters that are invisible or look broken; stop or route names may look odd in apps.
ARC_021.action: Retype the affected names and texts in your scheduling software.

ARC_022.title: Very large file
ARC_022.what: A file has more than one million rows. This is not an error; some apps may take longer to process it.

ARC_023.title: A ZIP inside the ZIP
ARC_023.what: The dataset file contains a second ZIP file; most apps do not read the inner file.
ARC_023.action: Put the GTFS files directly into a single ZIP. This is a file format issue; tell the export software vendor or your IT team.

ARC_024.title: GTFS files are not at the top of the archive
ARC_024.what: The GTFS files sit in a subfolder of the ZIP, so some apps may not be able to read them.
ARC_024.action: Move the GTFS files to the top level of the ZIP.

ARC_025.title: A required field is missing from the file
ARC_025.what: The header of {file} does not contain the {field} field.
ARC_025.action: Add the missing required field to the file.

ARC_026.title: Broken line endings in a file
ARC_026.what: Line endings in a file are not standard; some apps may merge rows.
ARC_026.action: This is a file format issue; tell the export software vendor or your IT team.

ARC_027.title: File read permission is off
ARC_027.what: A file inside the ZIP has its read permission turned off; some systems may not open it.
ARC_027.action: Package the dataset again. This is a file format issue; tell the export software vendor or your IT team.

ARC_028.title: Publication address does not end in .zip
ARC_028.what: The web address where the dataset is published does not end in a .zip file name; some apps may not recognise it as a dataset.
ARC_028.action: Publish the dataset at a permanent address ending in ".zip".

ARC_029.title: File exceeded the safety limit
ARC_029.what: The ZIP file grew abnormally while being opened; processing was stopped for safety.
ARC_029.action: Export the dataset again and retry. This is a file format issue; tell the export software vendor or your IT team.

ARC_030.title: Tab or line break inside text
ARC_030.what: A field value contains a tab or line break; the text may appear split in apps.
ARC_030.action: Retype the name or description on a single line.

ARC_031.title: Feed information is missing while translations are used
ARC_031.what: A translations file is present, but the dataset language is not specified.
ARC_031.action: Add the dataset information and specify the feed language.

ARC_032.title: HTML code inside text
ARC_032.what: A name or description contains an HTML tag or escape code (e.g. &); riders see it as code.
ARC_032.action: Enter the text again as plain text.

ARC_033.title: Unescaped quote in text
ARC_033.what: A field value contains a quote or comma that is not properly quoted; the row may be split wrongly.
ARC_033.action: This is a file format issue; tell the export software vendor or your IT team.

ARC_034.title: Header row repeated in the middle of the file
ARC_034.what: The header row appears again as a data row; this usually happens when two files are merged.
ARC_034.action: Export in one go. This is a file format issue; tell the export software vendor or your IT team.

ARC_035.title: Required file is empty
ARC_035.what: {file} exists but contains no usable data.
ARC_035.action: Add the required records to the file.

ARC_036.title: Inconsistent ZIP structure
ARC_036.what: The ZIP file opens in some tools and may not open in others.
ARC_036.action: Package the dataset again with a standard ZIP tool. This is a file format issue; tell the export software vendor or your IT team.

ARC_037.title: Accented or special characters in a code
ARC_037.what: A code (stop, route or trip identifier) contains accented letters or special characters; some apps cannot match these codes.
ARC_037.action: Use only English letters, digits and simple symbols in codes.

ARS_001.title: Same fare area code used twice
ARS_001.what: Two fare areas carry the same code.
ARS_001.action: Give each fare area a unique code.

ARS_002.title: Fare area code is empty
ARS_002.what: A fare area has an empty code.
ARS_002.action: Give each fare area a unique code.

ATR_001.title: Attribution record has no code
ATR_001.what: An attribution record, which credits contributors to the data, has an empty code.
ATR_001.action: Give each attribution record a unique code.

ATR_002.title: Attributed organisation has no name
ATR_002.what: An attribution record has no organisation name.
ATR_002.action: Enter the name of the organisation being credited.

ATR_003.title: Attribution record has no role
ATR_003.what: An attribution record does not say whether the organisation is the data producer, the operator or the authority.
ATR_003.action: Set at least one role for the organisation.

ATR_004.title: Data producer role invalid
ATR_004.what: The "data producer" value in an attribution record is not yes or no.
ATR_004.action: Set the value to yes or no.

ATR_005.title: Operator role invalid
ATR_005.what: The "operator" value in an attribution record is not yes or no.
ATR_005.action: Set the value to yes or no.

ATR_006.title: Authority role invalid
ATR_006.what: The "authority" value in an attribution record is not yes or no.
ATR_006.action: Set the value to yes or no.

ATR_007.title: Attribution web address invalid
ATR_007.what: The web address in an attribution record is not valid.
ATR_007.action: Enter a full address starting with "https://", or leave it empty.

ATR_008.title: Attribution e-mail invalid
ATR_008.what: The e-mail in an attribution record is not valid.
ATR_008.action: Enter the e-mail as name@domain.com, or leave it empty.

ATR_009.title: Attribution linked to more than one target
ATR_009.what: An attribution record is linked to an operator, a route and a trip at the same time; only one is allowed.
ATR_009.action: Link the attribution to just one operator, route or trip.

ATR_010.title: Attribution operator not found
ATR_010.what: An attribution record is linked to an operator that is not in the list.
ATR_010.action: Link the attribution to an existing operator.

ATR_011.title: Attribution route not found
ATR_011.what: An attribution record is linked to a route that is not in the list.
ATR_011.action: Link the attribution to an existing route.

ATR_012.title: Attribution trip not found
ATR_012.what: An attribution record is linked to a trip that is not in the list.
ATR_012.action: Link the attribution to an existing trip.

BKR_001.title: Previous-day booking setting in the wrong place
BKR_001.what: The last booking day and time for previous-day booking are set on a rule whose booking type is not "previous day".
BKR_001.action: Use these settings only on "previous day" booking rules.

BKR_003.title: Booking start time set without a day
BKR_003.what: The time the booking window opens is set, but not how many days before it opens.
BKR_003.action: Enter how many days before the booking opens, or remove the time.

BKR_004.title: Advance notice set on an immediate booking rule
BKR_004.what: A rule defined as immediate (real-time) booking has advance notice durations set.
BKR_004.action: Remove the advance notice durations or correct the booking type.

BKR_005.title: Maximum notice in the wrong place
BKR_005.what: The maximum advance notice can only be used for same-day booking; here it is set on a previous-day rule.
BKR_005.action: Remove this duration or change the booking type to "same day".

BKR_006.title: Minimum notice invalid
BKR_006.what: The minimum advance notice is not a number, or is zero or negative.
BKR_006.action: Enter the duration in minutes as a positive whole number.

BKR_007.title: Same-day booking has no notice time
BKR_007.what: A same-day booking rule does not say how many minutes before the trip a booking must be made.
BKR_007.action: Enter the minimum advance notice in minutes.

BKR_008.title: Previous-day booking has no last day
BKR_008.what: A previous-day booking rule does not say how many days before the trip booking closes.
BKR_008.action: Enter how many days before the trip booking closes.

BKR_009.title: Previous-day booking has no last time
BKR_009.what: A previous-day booking rule does not say until what time on the last day bookings are accepted.

BKR_010.title: Booking start day set without a time
BKR_010.what: How many days before the booking opens is set, but not at what time.
BKR_010.action: Enter the time the booking opens.

BKR_011.title: Booking window is reversed
BKR_011.what: The day booking closes is earlier than the day it opens; the window never opens.
BKR_011.action: Check that the opening day is the same as or earlier than the closing day.

BKR_012.title: Minute notice on a previous-day rule
BKR_012.what: A previous-day booking rule has a notice duration in minutes; this is only used on same-day rules.
BKR_012.action: Remove this duration or correct the booking type.

BKR_013.title: Last booking time set without a day
BKR_013.what: The last booking time is set, but not how many days before.
BKR_013.action: Enter the last booking day, or remove the time.

BKR_014.title: Booking calendar in the wrong place
BKR_014.what: The service calendar used to count booking days can only be used on previous-day rules; here it is set on another type.
BKR_014.action: Remove the calendar or change the booking type to "previous day".

BKR_015.title: Booking calendar not found
BKR_015.what: A booking rule is linked to a service calendar that is not defined.
BKR_015.action: Link the rule to an existing calendar, or leave the calendar empty.

BKR_016.title: Booking type missing or invalid
BKR_016.what: The booking rule type (immediate, same day, previous day) is missing or invalid.

BKR_017.title: Pickup booking rule not found
BKR_017.what: A demand-responsive stop is linked to a pickup booking rule that is not defined.
BKR_017.action: Link the stop to an existing booking rule, or define the rule.

BKR_018.title: Drop-off booking rule not found
BKR_018.what: A demand-responsive stop is linked to a drop-off booking rule that is not defined.
BKR_018.action: Link the stop to an existing booking rule, or define the rule.

BKR_019.title: Booking rule code empty or repeated
BKR_019.what: A booking rule has an empty code or the same code as another rule.
BKR_019.action: Give each booking rule a unique code.

BKR_020.title: Booking web address invalid
BKR_020.what: The web address for making bookings is not valid.
BKR_020.action: Enter a full address starting with "https://".

BKR_021.title: Booking information page invalid
BKR_021.what: The address of the booking information page is not valid.
BKR_021.action: Enter a full address starting with "https://", or leave it empty.

BKR_022.title: Booking phone invalid
BKR_022.what: The booking phone number does not look like a callable number.
BKR_022.action: Enter only the phone number; put any explanation in another field.

BKR_023.title: Booking duration is not a whole number
BKR_023.what: One of the booking day or minute values is not a whole number.
BKR_023.action: Enter these values as whole numbers.

BKR_024.title: Conflicting day setting on same-day booking
BKR_024.what: A same-day booking rule has a maximum notice and also says how many days before booking opens.
BKR_024.action: Remove one of the two settings.

BKR_025.title: Booking time invalid
BKR_025.what: The booking opening or closing time is not a valid time.

CAL_001.title: Same calendar code used twice
CAL_001.what: Two service calendars carry the same code; which days trips run becomes unclear.
CAL_001.action: Give each service calendar a unique code.

CAL_002.title: Invalid day value in calendar
CAL_002.what: Whether a day runs is written with a value other than yes/no.
CAL_002.action: Set each day to running or not running.

CAL_003.title: Calendar start date missing or invalid
CAL_003.what: The calendar start date is missing or cannot be read.
CAL_003.action: Enter the start date (YYYYMMDD in the export, e.g. 20260101).

CAL_004.title: Calendar end date missing or invalid
CAL_004.what: The calendar end date is missing or cannot be read.
CAL_004.action: Enter the end date (YYYYMMDD in the export, e.g. 20261231).

CAL_005.title: Calendar ends before it starts
CAL_005.what: The calendar end date is before its start date; the calendar never runs.
CAL_005.action: Check and correct the start and end dates.

CAL_006.title: No weekday ticked in the calendar
CAL_006.what: All days of the week are set to "not running". The calendar may run only on specific dates.
CAL_006.action: If it runs only on specific dates this is fine; otherwise tick the days it runs.

CAL_007.title: Long gap in the service period
CAL_007.what: A service calendar has a period of more than two weeks without any running day.
CAL_007.action: If the gap is planned (e.g. summer break) this is fine; otherwise add the missing days.

CAL_008.title: Calendar ends soon
CAL_008.what: A service calendar’s last day is approaching; after that date its trips will not be shown to riders.
CAL_008.action: Plan to prepare and publish the next timetable.

CAL_009.title: All service calendars have ended
CAL_009.what: All service periods in the dataset are in the past.
CAL_009.action: Add a calendar with current dates or update the existing one.

CAL_010.title: Calendar has very few running days
CAL_010.what: A service calendar runs on only a few days.
CAL_010.action: If it is a short-term service (e.g. an event) this is fine; otherwise check the calendar dates.

CAL_011.title: Unused service calendar
CAL_011.what: No trip uses this service calendar.
CAL_011.action: Link the calendar to trips, or delete it if unused.

CAL_012.title: Service gap in the near future
CAL_012.what: Within the next 30 days a calendar enters a period of more than two weeks without running days.
CAL_012.action: If the gap is planned this is fine; otherwise check the calendar.

CAL_013.title: All days of a service calendar are in the past
CAL_013.what: All running days of a service calendar are in the past; trips using it are no longer shown.
CAL_013.action: Update the calendar with new dates, or remove it if no longer used.

CAL_014.title: Calendar outside the dataset validity period
CAL_014.what: A calendar’s dates extend beyond the validity period declared for the dataset; apps may not trust those days.
CAL_014.action: Align the dataset validity period and the calendar dates.

CAL_015.title: All calendars start in the future
CAL_015.what: No calendar runs today; all start at a later date. No trips may be shown in rider apps today.
CAL_015.action: If you are publishing the new timetable early this is fine; otherwise check the start dates.

CAL_016.title: Service extends very far into the future
CAL_016.what: Calendars appear to run more than two years ahead; the real timetable period is probably shorter.
CAL_016.action: Set the calendar end to the last date the timetable is actually valid.

CAL_017.title: Calendar has not started yet
CAL_017.what: A service calendar starts at a later date. This is for information.
CAL_017.action: If prepared for the next period this is fine; otherwise check the start date.

CAL_018.title: Calendar has no running days at all
CAL_018.what: No weekday is ticked in a calendar and no special running dates are added.
CAL_018.action: Tick the days the calendar runs or add its special running dates.

CAL_020.title: Dataset validity exceeds 5 years
CAL_020.what: The validity period in the dataset information is longer than 5 years.
CAL_020.action: Limit the validity period to the dates the timetable is really valid.

CAL_021.title: No trips in the coming days
CAL_021.what: The calendar covers today, but has no running day in the next few days.
CAL_021.action: If it is a planned break this is fine; otherwise add the near dates.

CAL_022.title: Calendar code is empty
CAL_022.what: A service calendar has an empty code; trips cannot be linked to it.
CAL_022.action: Give the calendar a unique code.

CAL_023.title: Calendar end date suspiciously far away
CAL_023.what: A calendar ends years from now (e.g. 2099); this is usually a placeholder rather than a real end date.
CAL_023.action: Enter the real last valid date of the timetable as the calendar end.

CAL_024.title: Calendar not running in the next 7 days
CAL_024.what: A service calendar has no running day in the next 7 days. This is for information.
CAL_024.action: If planned (e.g. a holiday-only calendar) this is fine; otherwise update the calendar.

CAL_025.title: A day value is empty in the calendar
CAL_025.what: Whether a weekday runs is left empty in a service calendar.
CAL_025.action: Set each day to running or not running.

CLD_001.title: Calendar code empty in a calendar change
CLD_001.what: A special date (added or removed) does not say which calendar it belongs to.
CLD_001.action: Link the special date to its calendar.

CLD_002.title: Calendar change date invalid
CLD_002.what: A special date record has no date or it cannot be read.

CLD_003.title: Calendar change type invalid
CLD_003.what: A special date record does not say whether service is added or removed that day, or the value is invalid.
CLD_003.action: Mark the date as "service added" or "service removed".

CLD_004.title: Calendar has no running days
CLD_004.what: The weekly calendar is not used and some calendars have no "service added" date; their trips never run.
CLD_004.action: Add running dates to these calendars.

CLD_005.title: Calendar change date is unreasonable
CLD_005.what: A special date is not between 2000 and 2099; it was probably entered wrongly.

CLD_006.title: Too many special dates in a calendar
CLD_006.what: A calendar has more than 60 special date records. This is for information.
CLD_006.action: Consider defining regular days with the weekly calendar and using special dates only for exceptions.

CLD_007.title: Calendar built almost entirely from exceptions
CLD_007.what: Most running days of a calendar are entered one by one as special dates. This is for information.
CLD_007.action: Consider defining regular days with the weekly calendar.

DQ_003.title: Route description missing
DQ_003.what: The description field that gives riders extra information is empty for routes.
DQ_003.action: If you wish, add a short description such as operating hours or a route note.

DQ_004.title: Route web page missing
DQ_004.what: No web page is given where riders can see route details. This is for information.
DQ_004.action: If the route has an information page, enter its address.

DQ_005.title: No valid service period
DQ_005.what: No calendar in the dataset runs from today onward; no trips will be shown in rider apps.
DQ_005.action: Add the current period’s calendars and publish the dataset again.

DQ_005b.title: No trip has stop times
DQ_005b.what: Trips are defined but none has stop times; no trips may be shown in rider apps.
DQ_005b.action: Add trip stop times to the export.

DQ_005c.title: Most stops have no location
DQ_005c.what: Most stops have no location; they cannot be shown on a map and journeys cannot be planned.
DQ_005c.action: Mark the stop locations in your scheduling software and export again.

DQ_006.title: Most trips have no route shape
DQ_006.what: Most trips are not linked to a route shape; apps draw routes as straight lines.
DQ_006.action: Add the route shapes to the export.

DQ_009.title: Trips have no stop times
DQ_009.what: Trips are defined but there are no stop times at all; no timetable can be built.
DQ_009.action: Add trip stop times to the export.

DQ_010.title: Unused operator
DQ_010.what: No route is linked to an operator in the operator list.
DQ_010.action: Link the operator’s routes, or remove it if unused.

DQ_011.title: Only one stop in the dataset
DQ_011.what: The dataset contains only one stop; no journey can be planned.
DQ_011.action: Add all stops to the export.

DQ_012.title: Routes have no operator
DQ_012.what: There are several operators but routes do not say which one runs them.
DQ_012.action: Link each route to the operator that runs it.

DQ_013.title: Very few trips
DQ_013.what: The dataset contains only one or two trips. This is for information.
DQ_013.action: Check that all trips were exported.

DQ_016.title: Extra spaces in values
DQ_016.what: Some names, codes or values have unnecessary spaces at the start or end; this can break matching and search.
DQ_016.action: Remove the extra spaces from the affected records.

DQ_017.title: Suspicious coordinates
DQ_017.what: Many stops appear at 0,0 (Gulf of Guinea); locations were not entered or placeholders were left.
DQ_017.action: Enter the real locations of these stops.

DQ_018.title: Name written entirely in CAPITALS
DQ_018.what: A name shown to riders (stop, route or headsign) is written entirely in capitals; it is harder to read in apps.
DQ_018.action: Write names in normal case (e.g. "Main Station" rather than "MAIN STATION"). Abbreviations and brand names are exempt.

DQ_019.title: Name written entirely in lowercase
DQ_019.what: A name shown to riders is written entirely in lowercase.
DQ_019.action: Write names in normal case (e.g. "Main Station" rather than "main station"). Deliberately lowercase brand names are exempt.

DQ_020.title: Trip headsigns are empty
DQ_020.what: Most trips have no headsign shown to riders.
DQ_020.action: Enter where each trip is going as its headsign.

DQ_021.title: The same code is repeated
DQ_021.what: In a list (stops, routes, trips, etc.) the same code is used by more than one record; links may point to the wrong record.
DQ_021.action: Give every record a unique code.

DQ_022.title: Most stops share the same name
DQ_022.what: More than 80% of stops are recorded with the same name; placeholders may have been used instead of real names.

FAR_001.title: Same fare code used twice
FAR_001.what: Two fares carry the same code.
FAR_001.action: Give each fare a unique code.

FAR_002.title: Fare amount missing or invalid
FAR_002.what: A fare has no price, a non-numeric price or a negative one.
FAR_002.action: Enter the fare as zero or a positive amount.

FAR_003.title: Currency missing or invalid
FAR_003.what: A fare has no currency or it is not a three-letter standard code.
FAR_003.action: Enter the currency as a three-letter code such as "EUR" or "TRY".

FAR_004.title: Payment time invalid
FAR_004.what: The value saying whether the fare is paid on board or before boarding is invalid.

FAR_005.title: Transfer allowance invalid
FAR_005.what: The value saying how many transfers the fare allows is invalid.
FAR_005.action: Enter the transfer allowance as 0, 1, 2 or unlimited (empty).

FAR_006.title: Transfer duration invalid
FAR_006.what: The transfer validity duration of the fare is not a number.
FAR_006.action: Enter the duration in seconds, or leave it empty.

FAR_008.title: Fare operator not found
FAR_008.what: A fare is linked to an operator that is not in the operator list.
FAR_008.action: Link the fare to an existing operator.

FAR_010.title: Two different fares for the same journey
FAR_010.what: Several different fares are defined for the same route and zones; it is unclear which one applies.
FAR_010.action: Keep a single fare for each route and zone combination.

FAR_011.title: Payment time is empty
FAR_011.what: A fare does not say when payment is made.

FAR_012.title: Fare code is empty
FAR_012.what: A fare has an empty code.
FAR_012.action: Give each fare a unique code.

FAR_013.title: Fare amount has the wrong number of decimals
FAR_013.what: The fare amount is not written with the currency’s number of decimals (e.g. 2 for EUR). This is for information.
FAR_013.action: Write the amount with the currency’s decimals (e.g. 17.50).

FIN_001.title: Dataset publisher has no name
FIN_001.what: The dataset information does not give the publishing organisation’s name.
FIN_001.action: Enter the name of the organisation publishing the dataset.

FIN_002.title: Publisher web address missing or invalid
FIN_002.what: The dataset information has no valid web address for the publisher.
FIN_002.action: Enter the organisation’s full web address starting with "https://".

FIN_003.title: Dataset language missing
FIN_003.what: The dataset information does not say which language names and texts are in, or the code is not recognised.
FIN_003.action: Enter the language with a standard code such as "en".

FIN_004.title: Default language invalid
FIN_004.what: The default language code in the dataset information is not recognised.
FIN_004.action: Enter a standard code such as "en", or leave it empty.

FIN_005.title: Dataset start date invalid
FIN_005.what: The dataset validity start date cannot be read.

FIN_006.title: Dataset end date invalid
FIN_006.what: The dataset validity end date cannot be read.

FIN_007.title: Dataset version missing
FIN_007.what: The dataset information has no version; it is impossible to tell which version is published.
FIN_007.action: Enter a version that increases with each release (e.g. a date or number).

FIN_008.title: Contact e-mail invalid
FIN_008.what: The contact e-mail given for the dataset is not valid.
FIN_008.action: Enter the e-mail as name@domain.com, or leave it empty.

FIN_009.title: Contact address invalid
FIN_009.what: The contact web address given for the dataset is not valid.
FIN_009.action: Enter a full address starting with "https://", or leave it empty.

FIN_010.title: Dataset validity date has passed
FIN_010.what: The validity end date in the dataset information is in the past; apps may not treat the dataset as current.
FIN_010.action: Publish the dataset again with current validity dates.

FIN_012.title: Dataset starts after it ends
FIN_012.what: The dataset validity start date is after its end date.
FIN_012.action: Correct the start and end dates.

FIN_013.title: Fare operator not given
FIN_013.what: Some fares do not say which operator they belong to. This is for information.
FIN_013.action: Link the fares to their operator.

FIN_014.title: Dataset validity dates missing
FIN_014.what: The dataset information has no validity start and end dates.
FIN_014.action: Enter the first and last day the timetable is valid.

FIN_015.title: More than one dataset information record
FIN_015.what: The dataset information file has more than one record; there must be only one.

FIN_016.title: Dataset is not valid yet
FIN_016.what: The dataset validity starts in the future; trips may not be shown to riders today.
FIN_016.action: If you are publishing the new timetable early this is fine; otherwise correct the start date.

FIN_017.title: Dataset valid until far in the future
FIN_017.what: The dataset validity ends more than two years from now.
FIN_017.action: Enter the real last valid day of the timetable as the end date.

FIN_018.title: No contact details for the dataset
FIN_018.what: The dataset information has neither an e-mail nor a contact page; people cannot report data problems to you.
FIN_018.action: Add a contact e-mail or page.

FIN_019.title: Dataset validity ends soon
FIN_019.what: The dataset validity end date is approaching.
FIN_019.action: Plan to prepare and publish the next timetable.

FIN_020.title: Dataset valid for less than 7 days
FIN_020.what: The dataset validity period is shorter than a week.
FIN_020.action: Enter validity dates that match the real timetable period.

FLG_001.title: Fare leg rule product not found
FLG_001.what: A fare leg rule is linked to a fare product that is not defined.
FLG_001.action: Link the rule to an existing fare product.

FLG_002.title: Fare leg rule network not found
FLG_002.what: A fare leg rule is linked to a route network that is not defined.
FLG_002.action: Link the rule to an existing network.

FLG_003.title: Fare rule start area not found
FLG_003.what: A fare leg rule is linked to an origin area that is not defined.
FLG_003.action: Link the rule to an existing fare area.

FLG_004.title: Fare rule end area not found
FLG_004.what: A fare leg rule is linked to a destination area that is not defined.
FLG_004.action: Link the rule to an existing fare area.

FLG_005.title: Fare rule start time period not found
FLG_005.what: A fare leg rule is linked to a time period (e.g. peak hours) that is not defined.
FLG_005.action: Link the rule to an existing time period.

FLG_006.title: Fare rule end time period not found
FLG_006.what: A fare leg rule is linked to a time period that is not defined.
FLG_006.action: Link the rule to an existing time period.

FLG_007.title: Fare rule priority invalid
FLG_007.what: The priority value that decides which rule applies when several match is invalid.
FLG_007.action: Enter the priority as 0 or a positive whole number.

FLG_008.title: Fare leg rule product is empty
FLG_008.what: A fare leg rule does not say which fare product applies.
FLG_008.action: Choose the fare product for the rule.

FLJ_001.title: First network missing in a leg join rule
FLJ_001.what: In the rule that counts two legs as one journey, the first route network is empty or not defined.
FLJ_001.action: Choose an existing route network for the rule.

FLJ_002.title: Second network missing in a leg join rule
FLJ_002.what: In the rule that counts two legs as one journey, the second route network is empty or not defined.
FLJ_002.action: Choose an existing route network for the rule.

FLJ_003.title: First stop missing in a leg join rule
FLJ_003.what: In the leg join rule the first stop is missing, not found, or not a stop/station.
FLJ_003.action: Enter both stops together, or leave both empty.

FLJ_004.title: Second stop missing in a leg join rule
FLJ_004.what: In the leg join rule the second stop is missing, not found, or not a stop/station.
FLJ_004.action: Enter both stops together, or leave both empty.

FMD_001.title: Same fare media code used twice
FMD_001.what: Two fare media (card, app, etc.) carry the same code.
FMD_001.action: Give each fare medium a unique code.

FMD_002.title: Fare media type invalid
FMD_002.what: The fare medium type (paper ticket, card, contactless card, app) is missing or invalid.

FMD_003.title: Card or app has no name
FMD_003.what: A transit card or mobile app fare medium has no name; riders cannot tell which card is accepted.
FMD_003.action: Enter the name of the card or app.

FMD_004.title: Fare media code is empty
FMD_004.what: A fare medium has an empty code.
FMD_004.action: Give each fare medium a unique code.

FPD_001.title: The same fare product is defined twice
FPD_001.what: The same product is defined twice with the same rider category and fare medium.

FPD_002.title: Product price missing or invalid
FPD_002.what: A fare product has no price or a non-numeric price.
FPD_002.action: Enter the price as a number (0 if free).

FPD_003.title: Product currency invalid
FPD_003.what: A fare product’s currency is not a three-letter standard code.
FPD_003.action: Enter the currency with a code such as "EUR" or "TRY".

FPD_004.title: Product fare medium not found
FPD_004.what: A fare product is linked to a fare medium (card, app, etc.) that is not defined.
FPD_004.action: Link the product to an existing fare medium.

FPD_005.title: Product rider category not found
FPD_005.what: A fare product is linked to a rider category that is not defined.
FPD_005.action: Link the product to an existing rider category.

FPD_007.title: Product price has the wrong number of decimals
FPD_007.what: The product price is not written with the currency’s number of decimals (e.g. 2 for EUR).
FPD_007.action: Write the price with the currency’s decimals (e.g. 17.50).

FRL_001.title: Fare rule’s fare not found
FRL_001.what: A fare rule is linked to a fare that is not defined.
FRL_001.action: Link the rule to an existing fare.

FRL_002.title: Fare rule’s route not found
FRL_002.what: A fare rule is linked to a route that is not in the route list.
FRL_002.action: Link the rule to an existing route.

FRL_003.title: Fare rule origin zone not found
FRL_003.what: A fare rule points to an origin zone that no stop uses.
FRL_003.action: Link the rule to a fare zone used by stops.

FRL_004.title: Fare rule destination zone not found
FRL_004.what: A fare rule points to a destination zone that no stop uses.
FRL_004.action: Link the rule to a fare zone used by stops.

FRL_005.title: Fare rule pass-through zone not found
FRL_005.what: A fare rule points to a pass-through zone that no stop uses.
FRL_005.action: Link the rule to a fare zone used by stops.

FRL_006.title: Fares are not linked to any route
FRL_006.what: Fares are defined but no rule says on which routes or zones they apply. This is normal for flat-fare systems.
FRL_006.action: With a single flat fare this is fine; if fares depend on route or zone, add fare rules.

FRL_007.title: Fare rule is not linked to anything
FRL_007.what: A fare rule specifies neither a route nor a zone; it applies to every journey.
FRL_007.action: Add the route or zone to the rule.

FRL_008.title: Some routes have no fare
FRL_008.what: Fare rules are defined for some routes but not others; riders cannot see the fare on those routes.
FRL_008.action: Add fare rules for routes without a fare.

FRL_009.title: Some zone pairs have no fare
FRL_009.what: On zone-based routes, no fare is defined for some origin–destination zone pairs.
FRL_009.action: Add fare rules for the missing zone pairs, or define a single fare per route.

FRQ_001.title: Frequency definition’s trip not found
FRQ_001.what: A frequency definition (every X minutes) is linked to a trip that is not in the trip list.
FRQ_001.action: Link the frequency definition to an existing trip.

FRQ_002.title: Frequency start time invalid
FRQ_002.what: The start time of the frequency period is missing or cannot be read.
FRQ_002.action: Enter the start time as HH:MM:SS.

FRQ_003.title: Frequency end time invalid
FRQ_003.what: The end time of the frequency period is missing or cannot be read.
FRQ_003.action: Enter the end time as HH:MM:SS.

FRQ_004.title: Headway missing
FRQ_004.what: The frequency period does not say how often trips run, or the value is invalid.
FRQ_004.action: Enter the headway in seconds (e.g. 600 for 10 minutes).

FRQ_005.title: Frequency period is reversed
FRQ_005.what: The frequency period ends before or at the same time it starts.
FRQ_005.action: Correct the start and end times.

FRQ_006.title: Headway very long
FRQ_006.what: The headway in the frequency period is unusually long.
FRQ_006.action: If the headway is correct this is fine; otherwise check it.

FRQ_007.title: Exact times setting invalid
FRQ_007.what: The value saying whether trips leave at exact times or approximately is invalid.

FRQ_008.title: Headway is zero
FRQ_008.what: The headway is zero; trips appear to leave back to back.
FRQ_008.action: Enter the headway in seconds as a positive value.

FRQ_009.title: Headway very short
FRQ_009.what: The headway is shorter than one minute.
FRQ_009.action: Check the headway; seconds may have been entered instead of minutes.

FRQ_010.title: Very frequent service
FRQ_010.what: Trips in the frequency period leave at very short intervals. This is for information.
FRQ_010.action: If deliberate this is fine; otherwise check the headway.

FRQ_011.title: Frequency periods overlap
FRQ_011.what: Two frequency periods of the same trip overlap; it is unclear which headway applies at that time.
FRQ_011.action: Arrange the periods so they do not overlap.

FRQ_012.title: Frequency end coincides with a departure
FRQ_012.what: The end time of an exact-times frequency period falls on a departure time; it is unclear whether the last trip runs.
FRQ_012.action: Set the end time after the last trip and before the next possible one.

FTR_001.title: Transfer fare type invalid
FTR_001.what: The type saying how the transfer fare is calculated is missing or invalid.

FTR_002.title: Transfer fare first leg group not found
FTR_002.what: A transfer fare rule starts from a leg group that is not defined.
FTR_002.action: Link the rule to an existing leg group.

FTR_003.title: Transfer fare second leg group not found
FTR_003.what: A transfer fare rule leads to a leg group that is not defined.
FTR_003.action: Link the rule to an existing leg group.

FTR_004.title: Transfer fare product not found
FTR_004.what: A transfer fare rule is linked to a fare product that is not defined.
FTR_004.action: Link the rule to an existing fare product.

FTR_005.title: Transfer time reference invalid
FTR_005.what: The point from which the transfer time is counted (boarding, alighting, etc.) is invalid.
FTR_005.action: Choose the reference from the defined options.

FTR_006.title: Transfer duration invalid
FTR_006.what: The duration for which the transfer fare is valid is not a number, or is zero.
FTR_006.action: Enter the duration in seconds as a positive value.

FTR_007.title: Transfer time reference without a duration
FTR_007.what: The reference for counting the transfer time is set, but the duration itself is not.
FTR_007.action: Enter the duration or remove the reference.

FTR_008.title: Transfer count invalid
FTR_008.what: The allowed number of transfers is neither unlimited (-1) nor a positive whole number.
FTR_008.action: Enter -1 (unlimited) or a positive whole number.

FTR_009.title: No transfer count within the same group
FTR_009.what: A transfer within the same leg group does not say how many transfers are allowed.
FTR_009.action: Enter the transfer count (-1 for unlimited).

FTR_010.title: Transfer count between different groups
FTR_010.what: A transfer between different leg groups has a transfer count; this is only used within the same group.

FTR_011.title: Transfer duration without a reference
FTR_011.what: A transfer fare duration is set, but not the point from which it is counted.
FTR_011.action: Choose the time reference or remove the duration.

GEO_002.title: Stop far from the rest of the network
GEO_002.what: A stop appears hundreds of kilometres away from the rest of the network; its location is probably wrong.
GEO_002.action: Check and correct the stop location.

GEO_006.title: Large jump in a shape
GEO_006.what: There is an unusually long gap between two consecutive points of a route shape; the line does not follow the road.
GEO_006.action: Redraw this part of the shape along the road.

GEO_007.title: Very large jump in a shape
GEO_007.what: There is a very long gap between two consecutive points of a route shape; a point may be in the wrong place.
GEO_007.action: Check and redraw this part of the shape.

GEO_009.title: Stop far from the shape
GEO_009.what: A stop is unusually far from the shape of its trips; on the map it appears off the road.
GEO_009.action: Correct the location of the stop or of the shape.

GEO_012.title: Several stops on top of each other
GEO_012.what: At least three stops are very close together in the same small area; they may be copies of the same stop.
GEO_012.action: Merge records that represent the same physical stop.

GEO_013.title: Geographic coverage of the network
GEO_013.what: A summary of the area covered by the stops. This is for information.

GEO_014.title: Network spreads over a very large area
GEO_014.what: Stops are spread over an area wider than 500 km.
GEO_014.action: For an intercity network this is fine; otherwise check the locations of the distant stops.

GEO_015.title: Stop outside Japan
GEO_015.what: In a dataset whose language is Japanese, some stops appear outside Japan.
GEO_015.action: If these stops are deliberately outside Japan this is fine; otherwise check their coordinates.

GEO_016.title: Stop at location 0,0
GEO_016.what: A stop’s location is entered as 0,0 (Gulf of Guinea); in reality it has no location.
GEO_016.action: Enter the real location of the stop.

GEO_017.title: Shape point at location 0,0
GEO_017.what: A route shape has a point at 0,0; the line stretches into the ocean.
GEO_017.action: Correct this shape point or export the shape again.

GEO_018.title: All stops in the same small area
GEO_018.what: All stops lie within 200 metres; the locations may be placeholders.
GEO_018.action: If the service really runs in one small area (e.g. a campus) this is fine; otherwise enter the real stop locations.

GEO_019.title: Stop location is rounded
GEO_019.what: A stop’s latitude and longitude are entered as whole numbers; the stop appears kilometres off.
GEO_019.action: Enter the location with at least 5 decimal places.

GEO_020.title: All points of a shape at the same place
GEO_020.what: All points of a route shape are at the same location; the map shows a single dot instead of a line.
GEO_020.action: Redraw the shape along the road.

GEO_021.title: Most stops share locations
GEO_021.what: More than 30% of stops share their location with another stop.
GEO_021.action: Enter the real stop locations and merge copies of the same stop.

GEO_022.title: Stop very close to a pole
GEO_022.what: A stop’s latitude exceeds 89 degrees; the location is probably wrong (latitude and longitude may be swapped).
GEO_022.action: Check and correct the stop location.

GGL_001.title: In-seat transfer not supported by Google
GGL_001.what: The transfer type where riders stay on board is not supported by Google Maps. If you do not publish to Google, this is not a problem.
GGL_001.action: If Google compatibility is needed, model this connection as a vehicle block (same vehicle).

GGL_002.title: Google card price invalid
GGL_002.what: The Google-specific card payment price is not a valid value.
GGL_002.action: If you use this field, enter zero or a positive price; otherwise leave it empty.

JPN_001.title: Kana reading of stop name missing
JPN_001.what: A stop with a Japanese name has no kana (ja-Hrkt) reading.
JPN_001.action: Add the kana reading of the stop name to the translations.

JPN_002.title: Office code not defined
JPN_002.what: A route or trip is linked to an office not in the office list (office_jp).
JPN_002.action: Link it to an existing office, or define the office.

JPN_003.title: Japanese operator information does not match
JPN_003.what: The GTFS-JP additional operator information is linked to an operator not in the operator list.
JPN_003.action: Match the additional information to an existing operator.

JPN_004.title: Translations file missing
JPN_004.what: The GTFS-JP dataset has no translations file carrying kana readings of stop names.
JPN_004.action: Add the translations file with kana readings of stop names.

JPN_005.title: Office has no name
JPN_005.what: An office in the office list (office_jp) has no name.

JPN_006.title: Fare information missing
JPN_006.what: The GTFS-JP dataset has no fare information, or different fares are not linked to routes.
JPN_006.action: Add the fares and the routes they apply to.

JPN_007.title: Dataset information file missing
JPN_007.what: The GTFS-JP dataset has no dataset information file with the publisher and language.
JPN_007.action: Add the dataset information (publisher, language "ja", version).

JPN_008.title: Kana reading of route name missing
JPN_008.what: A route with a Japanese name has no kana reading.
JPN_008.action: Add the kana reading of the route name to the translations.

JPN_009.title: Kana reading of headsign missing
JPN_009.what: A headsign written in Japanese has no kana reading.
JPN_009.action: Add the kana reading of the headsign to the translations.

JPN_010.title: Kana reading of operator name missing
JPN_010.what: An operator with a Japanese name has no kana reading.
JPN_010.action: Add the kana reading of the operator name to the translations.

JPN_011.title: Operator code missing
JPN_011.what: In GTFS-JP the operator code, and the operator link on routes, are required even with a single operator; they are missing.
JPN_011.action: Give the operator a code and link all routes to it.

JPN_012.title: Code missing in Japanese operator information
JPN_012.what: The operator code is empty in the GTFS-JP additional operator information.
JPN_012.action: Link the additional information using the operator’s code.

JPN_013.title: Postal code format wrong
JPN_013.what: The operator’s postal code is not seven digits.
JPN_013.action: Enter the postal code as seven digits without a hyphen.

JPN_014.title: Office code empty or repeated
JPN_014.what: The office list has a record whose code is empty or the same as another office.
JPN_014.action: Give each office a unique code.

JPN_015.title: Legacy route information does not match
JPN_015.what: In the legacy route information (routes_jp) the route code is empty, repeated or not in the route list.
JPN_015.action: Link the route information uniquely to existing routes.

JPN_016.title: Route update date invalid
JPN_016.what: The update date in the route pattern or route information is not a valid date.

JPN_017.title: Trip pattern code empty or repeated
JPN_017.what: The trip pattern list (pattern_jp) has a record whose code is empty or repeated.
JPN_017.action: Give each pattern a unique code.

JPN_018.title: Trip pattern not found
JPN_018.what: A trip is linked to a trip pattern that is not in the pattern list.
JPN_018.action: Link the trip to an existing pattern.

JPN_019.title: Kana translation linked to the wrong record
JPN_019.what: A kana reading is linked to a missing or wrong record.
JPN_019.action: Match the kana reading to the correct stop, route or trip record.

JPN_020.title: Office web address or phone looks wrong
JPN_020.what: The office web address or phone does not look valid.
JPN_020.action: Enter a valid web address and a callable phone number.

JPN_021.title: Kana translation empty or conflicting
JPN_021.what: A kana reading is empty, there are two different readings for the same record, or the reading contains no kana.
JPN_021.action: Keep one reading per record, written in kana.

JPN_022.title: Required GTFS-JP v4 information missing
JPN_022.what: One of the items required in GTFS-JP v4 (operator language, dataset dates, version or stop type) is missing.

JPN_023.title: Dataset language is not Japanese
JPN_023.what: In the GTFS-JP profile the dataset language must be "ja", but something else is entered.

JPN_024.title: Operator language is not Japanese
JPN_024.what: In the GTFS-JP profile the operator language must be "ja", but something else is entered.

JPN_025.title: Operator time zone is not Tokyo
JPN_025.what: In the GTFS-JP profile the operator time zone must be Asia/Tokyo, but something else is entered.
JPN_025.action: Set the time zone to Asia/Tokyo.

JPN_026.title: Fare currency is not yen
JPN_026.what: In the GTFS-JP profile fares must be in JPY, but another currency is entered.

JPN_027.title: Route type is not bus
JPN_027.what: In the GTFS-JP v3 bus profile a route type other than bus is entered.
JPN_027.action: Choose "bus" for bus routes; use the appropriate profile for multimodal data.

JPN_028.title: Required kana reading missing
JPN_028.what: In GTFS-JP v3 kana readings are required for Japanese names, descriptions and headsigns; some are missing.
JPN_028.action: Add the missing kana readings to the translations.

JPN_029.title: Recommended kana reading missing
JPN_029.what: In GTFS-JP v4 kana readings are recommended for stop headsign text and attribution organisation names; some are missing.
JPN_029.action: Add kana readings for these texts to the translations.

JPN_030.title: Required Japanese translation row missing
JPN_030.what: In GTFS-JP v3 a translation row in "ja" is also required next to the kana reading; some are missing.

JPN_031.title: No fare zone at a zone-fare stop
JPN_031.what: A stop on a route with zone-based fares has no fare zone.
JPN_031.action: Match the stop’s fare zone to the zones in the route’s fare rules.

JPN_032.title: Operator code is not a corporate number
JPN_032.what: In GTFS-JP v3 the operator code must be the 13-digit corporate number (法人番号).
JPN_032.action: Enter the operator code as the 13-digit corporate number.

JPN_033.title: Custom name uses the "jp" namespace
JPN_033.what: A custom file or field name uses the "jp" prefix or suffix reserved for GTFS-JP.
JPN_033.action: Rename the custom file or field without "jp".

LOC_001.title: Service area shape invalid
LOC_001.what: One of the demand-responsive service areas is not drawn as an area (polygon).
LOC_001.action: Redraw the service area as a closed area.

LOC_002.title: Service area has no shape
LOC_002.what: One of the demand-responsive service areas has no drawing.
LOC_002.action: Draw the service area on the map.

LOC_003.title: Service area has no code
LOC_003.what: A demand-responsive service area has no code; trips cannot be linked to it.
LOC_003.action: Give each service area a unique code.

LOC_004.title: Service area is not closed
LOC_004.what: A service area’s boundary does not end where it starts; the area is not closed.
LOC_004.action: Close the boundary at its starting point.

LOC_005.title: Service area file is empty
LOC_005.what: The service areas file exists but contains no area.
LOC_005.action: If you use demand-responsive service, add the areas; otherwise remove the file.

LOC_006.title: Service area is very large
LOC_006.what: A service area is larger than 500 km²; the real service area is probably smaller.
LOC_006.action: Shrink the area to the real service area or split it into several areas.

LOC_007.title: Same service area code used twice
LOC_007.what: Two service areas carry the same code.
LOC_007.action: Give each area a unique code.

LOC_008.title: Service area record format wrong
LOC_008.what: A record in the service areas file has a missing or wrong type.
LOC_008.action: This is a file format issue; tell the export software vendor or your IT team.

LOC_009.title: Service area record has no properties
LOC_009.what: A record in the service areas file is missing its properties section.
LOC_009.action: This is a file format issue; tell the export software vendor or your IT team.

LOC_010.title: Service area has no coordinates
LOC_010.what: A service area has a shape but its corner coordinates are missing; it cannot be drawn.
LOC_010.action: Redraw the service area on the map.

LOC_011.title: Service area crosses itself
LOC_011.what: A service area’s boundary crosses itself, or a hole extends outside the area.
LOC_011.action: Redraw the boundary so it does not cross itself.

LOC_012.title: Service area file cannot be read
LOC_012.what: The service areas file is not a valid map file (GeoJSON).
LOC_012.action: Export the service areas again. This is a file format issue; tell the export software vendor or your IT team.

LVL_001.title: Same level code used twice
LVL_001.what: Two level records carry the same code.
LVL_001.action: Give each level a unique code, or merge the duplicates.

LVL_002.title: Level order invalid
LVL_002.what: The number giving the level’s position relative to ground cannot be read.
LVL_002.action: Enter the level order as a number (ground 0, upper levels positive, lower levels negative).

LVL_003.title: Level has no name
LVL_003.what: A level has no name to show riders.

LVL_004.title: Unused level
LVL_004.what: A level is defined but no stop or platform is on it.
LVL_004.action: Link the level to the relevant stops, or delete it.

LVL_005.title: Level name too long
LVL_005.what: A level name is longer than 255 characters.

LVL_006.title: Level missing at an elevator connection
LVL_006.what: One of the points an elevator connects does not say which level it is on.
LVL_006.action: Assign levels to the points at both ends of the elevator.

LVL_007.title: Level order is empty
LVL_007.what: A level has no order value.
LVL_007.action: Enter the level order as a number.

LVL_008.title: Level code is empty
LVL_008.what: A level has an empty code.
LVL_008.action: Give each level a unique code.

NET_001.title: Same network code used twice
NET_001.what: Two route networks carry the same code.
NET_001.action: Give each network a unique code, or merge the duplicates.

NET_002.title: Network not found in route–network link
NET_002.what: A route is assigned to an empty or undefined network.
NET_002.action: Assign the route to an existing network.

NET_003.title: Route not found in route–network link
NET_003.what: A network is assigned a route that is empty or not in the route list.
NET_003.action: Assign an existing route to the network.

NET_004.title: Network code is empty
NET_004.what: A route network has an empty code.
NET_004.action: Give each network a unique code.

OPR_001.title: Long gap between trips on a route
OPR_001.what: On a route, the time between two trips in the same direction and day is unusually long.
OPR_001.action: If the gap is planned this is fine; otherwise add the missing trips.

OPR_003.title: Trips bunched very closely
OPR_003.what: Two trips on the same route, direction and day leave very close together; the same trip may have been entered twice.
OPR_003.action: Check the times of these two trips; delete one if it is a duplicate.

OPR_004.title: No weekend trips
OPR_004.what: This route has no trips at the weekend. This is for information.
OPR_004.action: If the route does not run at weekends this is fine; otherwise check the weekend calendar.

OPR_005.title: Unusual service frequency
OPR_005.what: A route’s headways are unusual compared with similar routes. This is for information.
OPR_005.action: No action needed; if unexpected, review the timetable.

OPR_006.title: Trip has too few stops
OPR_006.what: This trip has fewer than two stops; riders cannot travel anywhere with it.
OPR_006.action: Add the missing stops to the trip, or delete the unused trip.

OPR_007.title: Stop pattern repeats within a trip
OPR_007.what: The same sequence of stops repeats within a trip. This is normal on loop routes.
OPR_007.action: If it is a loop route this is fine; otherwise check the trip’s stop order.

OPR_008.title: Excessive speed in several parts of a trip
OPR_008.what: The speed in more than one part of a trip is far above what is expected.
OPR_008.action: Check the trip’s stop times and the stop locations together.

OPR_009.title: Night trip starts very late
OPR_009.what: Some trips leave after 23:00. This is for information.
OPR_009.action: If night service is planned this is fine; otherwise check the departure times and calendar.

OPR_010.title: Conflicting accessibility on a route
OPR_010.what: Some trips on the same route are marked accessible or bike-friendly and others are not.
OPR_010.action: If different vehicles are used this is fine; otherwise mark the route’s trips consistently.

OPR_011.title: Calendar never runs
OPR_011.what: A calendar used by trips has no running day; these trips may not be shown in rider apps.
OPR_011.action: Add running days to the calendar.

OPR_012.title: Service gap in a calendar
OPR_012.what: A calendar used by trips has a long gap between running days.
OPR_012.action: If the gap is planned this is fine; otherwise add the missing running days.

OPR_013.title: Route runs in one direction only
OPR_013.what: This route only has trips in one direction. This is for information.
OPR_013.action: If the route is one-way or a loop this is fine; otherwise add the opposite-direction trips.

OPR_014.title: Long transfer times
OPR_014.what: The average minimum transfer time of defined transfers exceeds 10 minutes.
OPR_014.action: Check the transfer times against real walking and waiting times.

OPR_015.title: Route uses the same shape in both directions
OPR_015.what: Outbound and return trips share a single route shape. This is for information.
OPR_015.action: If the two directions use different roads, use a separate shape for each direction.

OPR_016.title: No running day in the whole dataset
OPR_016.what: There are trips but no calendar has a single running day; no trips will be shown to riders.
OPR_016.action: Add running days to the calendars.

OPR_017.title: Trip distance very short
OPR_017.what: A trip’s total distance is unusually short.
OPR_017.action: Check the trip’s shape and stop locations; if it really is a short service this is fine.

OPR_019.title: Two calendars running on the same day on a route
OPR_019.what: More than one service calendar is active on the same day on a route; trips may appear twice.
OPR_019.action: For example, switch off the normal calendar and switch on the holiday calendar on a holiday; if both are meant to run together this is fine.

OPR_020.title: Two calendars overlap on a special day
OPR_020.what: On a special day both the normal and the special calendar run on a route.
OPR_020.action: Switch off the normal calendar on that day (remove it as an exception).

OPR_021.title: Normal calendar also runs on a special day
OPR_021.what: The special-day calendar is active but the normal calendar was not switched off that day; trips appear twice.
OPR_021.action: Switch off the normal calendar on that day as an exception.

OPR_022.title: Special-day calendar not activated
OPR_022.what: On the defined special day the normal calendar runs but the special calendar is not switched on.
OPR_022.action: Add the special-day calendar on that day as an exception.

OPR_023.title: No calendar runs during the special period
OPR_023.what: During the defined special period neither the normal nor the special calendar runs; there are no trips on those days.
OPR_023.action: Switch on either the normal or the special calendar for those days.

OPR_024.title: More than 500 trips on a route
OPR_024.what: More than 500 trips are defined on a route for one calendar; several routes may have been merged.
OPR_024.action: Check that trips are linked to the right route.

OPR_025.title: Trips last less than a minute on average
OPR_025.what: The average trip duration in the dataset is under 60 seconds; times were probably exported wrongly.
OPR_025.action: Check that trip stop times were exported correctly.

PDW_006.title: Demand-responsive windows overlap
PDW_006.what: Two pickup/drop-off windows overlap for the same area on the same trip.
PDW_006.action: Arrange the windows so they do not overlap.

PTH_001.title: Same walking connection code used twice
PTH_001.what: Two in-station walking connections carry the same code.
PTH_001.action: Give each walking connection a unique code.

PTH_002.title: Walking connection start point not found
PTH_002.what: An in-station walking connection starts at a point not in the stop list.
PTH_002.action: Link its start to an existing platform, entrance or generic node.

PTH_003.title: Walking connection end point not found
PTH_003.what: An in-station walking connection ends at a point not in the stop list.
PTH_003.action: Link its end to an existing platform, entrance or generic node.

PTH_004.title: Walking connection type invalid
PTH_004.what: The type of walking connection (walkway, stairs, moving sidewalk, escalator, elevator, fare gate, exit gate) is not a defined value.

PTH_005.title: Walking connection direction invalid
PTH_005.what: Whether the walking connection is one-way or two-way is missing or invalid.
PTH_005.action: Mark the walking connection as one-way or two-way.

PTH_006.title: Walking connection length invalid
PTH_006.what: The length of the walking connection is not a number or is negative.
PTH_006.action: Enter the length in metres as a positive number, or leave it empty.

PTH_007.title: Traversal time invalid
PTH_007.what: The time to pass through the walking connection is not a number or is zero.
PTH_007.action: Enter the traversal time in seconds as a positive whole number, or leave it empty.

PTH_008.title: Number of stairs missing
PTH_008.what: A walking connection defined as stairs has no step count; this matters for riders with reduced mobility.

PTH_009.title: Walkway slope missing
PTH_009.what: A walkway has no slope information; this matters for wheelchair users.

PTH_010.title: Walking connection width invalid
PTH_010.what: The minimum width of the walking connection is not a number, or is zero or negative.
PTH_010.action: Enter the width in metres as a positive number, or leave it empty.

PTH_011.title: Walking connection returns to the same point
PTH_011.what: A walking connection ends where it starts; it leads nowhere.
PTH_011.action: Link its start and end to two different points.

PTH_012.title: Connection missing between station entrance and platform
PTH_012.what: There is no continuous walking connection from the station entrance to the platform; riders cannot see how to reach it.
PTH_012.action: Add the missing walking connections from entrances to platforms.

PTH_013.title: Accessible route analysis
PTH_013.what: Checks whether the station has a route from entrance to platform suitable for wheelchairs in slope and width. This is for information.
PTH_013.action: If there is an accessible route, enter its slope and width information.

PTH_014.title: Walking connection joins two different stations
PTH_014.what: An in-station walking connection links points belonging to two different stations.
PTH_014.action: First check that both ends are attached to the right station. If there really is a walkway between the two stations, this may be deliberate.

PTH_015.title: Walking connection time too short for its distance
PTH_015.what: The length and traversal time of a walking connection mean walking faster than 3 metres per second.
PTH_015.action: Correct the length and traversal time to real values.

PTH_016.title: Exit gate is two-way
PTH_016.what: A fare gate meant only for exiting is defined as two-way.

PTH_017.title: Slope value invalid
PTH_017.what: The slope is not a number, or it is entered on a walking connection where slope makes no sense (stairs, elevator, etc.).
PTH_017.action: Enter the slope as a number only on walkways and moving sidewalks.

PTH_018.title: Walking connection sign text too long
PTH_018.what: The sign text riders see on a walking connection is longer than 255 characters.
PTH_018.action: Enter the short text shown on the sign.

PTH_019.title: Dead-end node
PTH_019.what: A node inside the station is connected to only one walking connection; it is impossible to continue from there.
PTH_019.action: Connect the node to at least two walking connections, or remove it.

PTH_020.title: Walking connection code is empty
PTH_020.what: An in-station walking connection has an empty code.
PTH_020.action: Give each walking connection a unique code.

PTH_021.title: Walking connection start is empty
PTH_021.what: A walking connection does not say where it starts.
PTH_021.action: Choose the start point of the walking connection.

PTH_022.title: Walking connection end is empty
PTH_022.what: A walking connection does not say where it ends.
PTH_022.action: Choose the end point of the walking connection.

PTH_023.title: Walking connection type is empty
PTH_023.what: A walking connection has no type.
PTH_023.action: Choose the walking connection type (walkway, stairs, elevator, etc.).

PTH_024.title: Walking connection direction is empty
PTH_024.what: A walking connection does not say whether it is one-way or two-way.
PTH_024.action: Mark the walking connection as one-way or two-way.

PTH_025.title: Walking connection length missing
PTH_025.what: Walkways, fare gates and exit gates have no length; walking time cannot be calculated.
PTH_025.action: Enter the length of these walking connections in metres.

PTH_026.title: Walking connection attached to the station itself
PTH_026.what: A walking connection is attached to the station itself; walking connections must attach to platforms, entrances or nodes.
PTH_026.action: Attach the walking connection to the relevant platform, entrance or node.

PTH_027.title: Step count invalid
PTH_027.what: The stair step count is zero or not a whole number.
PTH_027.action: Enter the step count as a whole number (positive going up, negative going down), or leave it empty.

PTH_028.title: Slope on the wrong connection type
PTH_028.what: Slope information is entered on a walking connection other than a walkway or moving sidewalk.
PTH_028.action: Use slope only on walkways and moving sidewalks.

PTH_029.title: Traversal time missing
PTH_029.what: A moving sidewalk, escalator or elevator has no traversal time.
PTH_029.action: Enter the traversal time of these walking connections in seconds.

PTH_030.title: Walking connection on a platform that has boarding areas
PTH_030.what: Boarding areas are defined for the platform, but the walking connection is attached directly to the platform.
PTH_030.action: Attach the walking connection to the relevant boarding area.

PTH_031.title: Walking connection to a street-access stop
PTH_031.what: A walking connection is attached to a stop that is reached directly from the street rather than through the station.
PTH_031.action: Set the stop’s access to "through the station", or remove this walking connection.

RCT_001.title: Same rider category code used twice
RCT_001.what: Two rider categories (e.g. student, senior) carry the same code.
RCT_001.action: Give each rider category a unique code.

RCT_002.title: Rider category has no name
RCT_002.what: A rider category has no name.

RCT_003.title: Default category value invalid
RCT_003.what: The value saying whether the rider category is the default is invalid.
RCT_003.action: Set the value to yes or no.

RCT_004.title: Age limit invalid
RCT_004.what: The minimum or maximum age of a rider category is not a whole number.
RCT_004.action: Enter age limits as whole numbers, or leave them empty.

RCT_005.title: Age range is reversed
RCT_005.what: A rider category’s maximum age is lower than its minimum age.

RCT_006.title: Not exactly one default category per product
RCT_006.what: A fare product has no default rider category, or more than one.
RCT_006.action: Make exactly one rider category the default for each product.

RCT_007.title: Category eligibility page invalid
RCT_007.what: The address of the page explaining the rider category conditions is not valid.
RCT_007.action: Enter a full address starting with "https://", or leave it empty.

RCT_008.title: Rider category code is empty
RCT_008.what: A rider category has an empty code.
RCT_008.action: Give each category a unique code.

RTS_001.title: Same route code used twice
RTS_001.what: Two different routes carry the same code; it becomes unclear which route trips belong to.
RTS_001.action: Give each route a unique code.

RTS_002.title: Route operator not found
RTS_002.what: A route is linked to an operator that is not in the operator list.
RTS_002.action: Link the route to an existing operator, or add the operator to the list.

RTS_003.title: Route has no name
RTS_003.what: A route has neither a short name (number) nor a long name; riders cannot recognise it.
RTS_003.action: Enter the route number or name.

RTS_004.title: Route vehicle type missing or invalid
RTS_004.what: The route type (bus, tram, metro, etc.) is missing or not a defined value.

RTS_005.title: Route web address invalid
RTS_005.what: The web address given for the route is not valid.
RTS_005.action: Enter a full address starting with "https://", or leave it empty.

RTS_006.title: Route colour invalid
RTS_006.what: The route colour is not a 6-digit colour code (e.g. FF0000).
RTS_006.action: Enter the route colour as a 6-digit colour code.

RTS_007.title: Route text colour invalid
RTS_007.what: The text colour on the route badge is not a 6-digit colour code (e.g. FFFFFF).
RTS_007.action: Enter the text colour as a 6-digit colour code.

RTS_008.title: Route badge hard to read
RTS_008.what: The contrast between the route colour and its text colour is low; the route number on the badge is hard to read.
RTS_008.action: Choose a text colour dark or light enough for the route colour (e.g. white text on a dark background).

RTS_010.title: Route number too long
RTS_010.what: The route short name is longer than 12 characters; it does not fit on badges and signs.
RTS_010.action: Put only the route number in the short name; move the description to the long name.

RTS_011.title: Route name too long
RTS_011.what: The route long name is longer than 100 characters; apps cut it off.
RTS_011.action: Shorten the route name; put details in the route description.

RTS_012.title: Route without trips
RTS_012.what: This route has no trips; it may appear as an empty route in rider apps.
RTS_012.action: If the route is not in service, remove it; if it is, add its trips.

RTS_013.title: Route continuous pickup value invalid
RTS_013.what: The value saying whether riders may board along the road between stops is not one of the defined options.
RTS_013.action: Choose the continuous pickup setting, or leave it empty if you do not use it.

RTS_016.title: Route has no running days
RTS_016.what: None of the calendars used by this route’s trips has a running day; the route may not be shown in rider apps.
RTS_016.action: Check the service calendars used by the route’s trips.

RTS_017.title: Route has no shape
RTS_017.what: None of this route’s trips has a route shape; apps draw it as straight lines between stops.
RTS_017.action: Add the route’s on-road shape to the export.

RTS_018.title: Route continuous drop-off value invalid
RTS_018.what: The value saying whether riders may alight along the road between stops is not one of the defined options.
RTS_018.action: Choose the continuous drop-off setting, or leave it empty if you do not use it.

RTS_019.title: Two routes have the same name
RTS_019.what: Several routes carry exactly the same number and name; riders cannot tell them apart in search.
RTS_019.action: If they are different services, give them distinctive names; if they are the same service, merge them.

RTS_020.title: Route page same as operator page
RTS_020.what: The web address given for the route is the operator’s general page.
RTS_020.action: If there is a route-specific page, enter it; otherwise leave the address empty.

RTS_021.title: Route number exceeds the Google Transit limit (6 characters)
RTS_021.what: The route short name is longer than 6 characters; Google Maps may cut it to fit the badge. If you do not publish to Google, this is not a problem.
RTS_021.action: If you publish to Google, put only the route number in the short name.

RTS_022.title: Route name repeats the number
RTS_022.what: The route long name also contains its number; apps show repetitions like "34 34 Centre".
RTS_022.action: Write only the itinerary in the long name, without the number (e.g. "Centre – University").

RTS_023.title: Route description same as its name
RTS_023.what: The route description repeats its long name; it gives riders no extra information.
RTS_023.action: Write extra information such as operating hours or a route note, or leave it empty.

RTS_024.title: Contactless payment value invalid
RTS_024.what: The value saying whether contactless payment is accepted on the route is not one of the defined options.

RTS_025.title: Route operator not given
RTS_025.what: Some routes have no operator; with a single operator this is still recommended.
RTS_025.action: Assign the operator to the routes.

RTS_026.title: Same route number on different routes
RTS_026.what: The same short name (number) is used on routes with different names; riders may be confused in search.
RTS_026.action: If the number is deliberately shared by variants this is fine; otherwise give the routes separate numbers.

RTS_027.title: Same route name on different routes
RTS_027.what: The same long name is used on routes with different numbers; riders cannot tell them apart in search.
RTS_027.action: If the name is deliberately shared this is fine; otherwise give each route a distinctive name.

RTS_028.title: Continuous boarding open on a demand-responsive route
RTS_028.what: A route with demand-responsive trips has boarding or alighting along the road switched on; the two cannot be combined.
RTS_028.action: Switch off continuous boarding and alighting on this route, or leave the setting empty.

RTS_029.title: Route sort order invalid
RTS_029.what: The value deciding the order routes appear in lists is negative or not a number.
RTS_029.action: Enter the sort order as 0 or a positive whole number, or leave it empty.

RTS_030.title: Route type uses an extended code
